content.text:
Phase 3 is complete. I added [the analysis script](/Users/chenfengru/LLM4Rec-Course-codex/week03/collaborative-filtering-movie-recommender/analysis/phase3.mjs) and [its protocol](/Users/chenfengru/LLM4Rec-Course-codex/week03/collaborative-filtering-movie-recommender/analysis/phase3_protocol.md). The application algorithms, teacher baseline, datasets, and Phase 2 evidence are unchanged. Nothing was committed or pushed.

**User 2’s scores near 5 are explained by the contributing ratings.** Every neighbor who contributed to each User-Based Top-5 candidate rated that movie **5**. A positive-weight average of those ratings is 5; three raw values are `5.000000000000001` because of floating-point rounding.

| User-Based movie ID | Score | Neighbors who rated it | Similarity-weight sum | Co-rated movies behind those similarities |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 187 | 5.000 | 2 | 1.995 | 2, 4 |
| 480 | 5.000 | 3 | 2.998 | 1, 2, 3 |
| 484 | 5.000 | 2 | 1.994 | 3, 4 |
| 17 | 5.000 | 1 | 1.000 | 1 |
| 27 | 5.000 | 1 | 1.000 | 2 |

The Item-Based Top-5 used **6, 10, 8, 13, and 7** contributing rated movies, with similarity-weight sums equal to those counts. Every contributing item–item similarity in those five predictions rested on **one co-rating** and therefore equaled 1. The full contributor records and reconstructed-score checks are in [user 2’s support results](/Users/chenfengru/LLM4Rec-Course-codex/week03/collaborative-filtering-movie-recommender/results/phase3_user2_support.json).

**Overlap reliability was measured across every unique unordered pair**, including pairs with zero overlap:

| Pairs | Count | 10th percentile | 25th | Median | ≤1 co-rating | ≤2 | ≤5 | ≤10 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| User–user | 444,153 | 2 | 4 | 10 | 8.42% | 14.29% | 31.64% | 52.78% |
| Item–item | 1,413,721 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 51.15% | 60.38% | 73.52% | 82.91% |

Among pairs with raw cosine **≥0.9**, there were 374,415 user pairs (median overlap 11; **11.94%** had at most two co-ratings) and 827,006 item pairs (median overlap 3; **47.70%** had at most two). Examples include users **1 and 88** and items **1 and 361**: each pair has cosine **1** from just **one** shared rating. The distributions and further examples are in [reliability results](/Users/chenfengru/LLM4Rec-Course-codex/week03/collaborative-filtering-movie-recommender/results/phase3_reliability.json).

For leave-one-out evaluation, **911 users** qualified: each had at least 21 ratings and a rating of 4 or 5 to hold out. I selected the latest positive rating by timestamp, using lower movie ID to break timestamp ties. Its matrix cell was zero during both calls and restored afterward. Hits used captured movie IDs, so duplicate titles could not create false matches. Candidate ties followed the existing code: descending score, then ascending movie ID.

| Method | Evaluated | Top-5 hits | HitRate@5 | MRR@5 | Fewer than 5 results |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| User-Based | 911 | 9 | 0.988% | 0.004848 | 0 |
| Item-Based | 911 | 0 | 0% | 0 | 0 |

The full [per-user evaluation results](/Users/chenfengru/LLM4Rec-Course-codex/week03/collaborative-filtering-movie-recommender/results/phase3_leave_one_out.json) include holdouts and ranks. A [ten-user rank check](/Users/chenfengru/LLM4Rec-Course-codex/week03/collaborative-filtering-movie-recommender/results/phase3_spotcheck.json) independently matched the Top-5 hit records: its Item-Based held-out items ranked **506–1,409**, while its Item-Based Top-5 movies were mostly rated by only one user.

**Theoretical pair counts and measured runtime are separate findings.** With 943 users, a full square has **889,249** user-pair positions, or **444,153** unique unordered pairs excluding self-pairs. With 1,682 items, those counts are **2,829,124** and **1,413,721**. An on-demand call does different work: User-Based makes 942 similarity calls; Item-Based makes \(r(1682-r)\) calls for a user with \(r\) rated movies.

Five fixed users received two warmups and five timed calls per method. Across the 25 measured calls per method, User-Based averaged **1.59 ms** (median **1.40 ms**); Item-Based averaged **388.48 ms** (median **332.31 ms**). For user 2, the per-call counts were 942 versus 100,440, and mean times were **1.32 ms** versus **135.66 ms**. Per-user measurements are in [efficiency results](/Users/chenfengru/LLM4Rec-Course-codex/week03/collaborative-filtering-movie-recommender/results/phase3_efficiency.json).

**No implementation defect was confirmed.** Sparse overlap and one-co-rating cosine values explain the observed high similarities and rankings under the chosen method; changing that method was outside this phase. The results support the stated overlap counts, this specific leave-one-out outcome, and the measured runtime difference for this implementation. They do **not** establish general recommendation quality, business impact, performance on other datasets, or how an alternative missing-value method would perform.

For a later Week 2 comparison, the [protocol](/Users/chenfengru/LLM4Rec-Course-codex/week03/collaborative-filtering-movie-recommender/analysis/phase3_protocol.md) proposes the same users and holdouts, a common unseen-movie candidate pool, and comparison by movie ID and held-out rank. Week 2’s genre cosine and Week 3’s predicted ratings cannot be compared as raw scores. Week 2 also uses one or three liked movies while Week 3 uses the remaining rating history, so that difference in available input would need to be stated or controlled.

I’ve stopped before any algorithm change or business analysis.

Phase 3 is accepted.

Now perform Phase 4 as ONE controlled improvement experiment.

Do not modify week03/teacher-baseline/.
Do not commit or push.
Do not change the datasets.
Do not add mean imputation, Pearson correlation, matrix factorization,
or unrelated UI changes.

Research question:
Can overlap-confidence weighting reduce the unreliability of raw
co-rated cosine similarities in this sparse MovieLens dataset?

Keep the current co-rated-only implementation as the BASELINE.

1. Implement an experimental overlap-weighted similarity

For two users/items with raw co-rated cosine s and n co-rated entries:
```r
weighted_similarity =
    s * min(n / T, 1)
```

Use T = 10 as the primary controlled setting.

Do not replace the baseline implementation yet.
Keep the weighted method isolated so baseline and improvement can be
evaluated side by side.

Explain clearly that the overlap factor is a confidence adjustment,
not an additional rating or an imputed value.

2. Re-run the exact same Phase 3 leave-one-out protocol

Use the same:

- 911 eligible users,
- most recent rating >= 4 as holdout,
- deterministic tie-breaking,
- Top-5,
- held-out matrix cell removed during prediction.

Evaluate four methods:

A. User-Based raw co-rated cosine
B. User-Based overlap-weighted cosine
C. Item-Based raw co-rated cosine
D. Item-Based overlap-weighted cosine

Report for each:

- HitRate\@5
- MRR\@5
- Top-5 hit count
- fewer-than-5 result count

3. Reliability diagnostics

For the weighted method, inspect whether Top-5 recommendations are
supported by more evidence.

For both User-Based and Item-Based, compare baseline vs weighted:

- median co-rated count behind contributing similarities,
- fraction of contributing similarities based on <=1, <=2, <=5 ratings,
- prediction support count,
- similarity-weight sum.

Re-run user 2 and show how its recommendations/scores/support change.

4. Sensitivity check

T=10 is the primary setting.

Also run a small sensitivity analysis for:
T = 5, 10, 20

Do not tune T on a hidden test set or select a winner solely because it
maximizes HitRate\@5.

Report all three settings transparently.

The purpose is to see whether the conclusion is stable, not to optimize
aggressively.

5. Efficiency

Measure whether overlap weighting materially changes runtime relative
to the raw implementation.

Use the same fixed users and benchmark protocol from Phase 3.

6. Interpretation rules

Do not claim improved recommendation quality unless the held-out metrics
actually improve.

Do not call raw cosine incorrect.
Describe it as mathematically valid but potentially low-confidence under
small overlap.

Do not claim overlap weighting solves cold start.

7. Outputs

Save new scripts/results separately under:
week03/collaborative-filtering-movie-recommender/analysis/
week03/collaborative-filtering-movie-recommender/results/

Do not overwrite Phase 3 outputs.

At the end report:

A. baseline vs weighted metrics,
B. T=5/10/20 sensitivity,
C. change in overlap support,
D. user 2 before/after,
E. runtime effect,
F. whether the improvement hypothesis was supported,
G. what still remains unresolved.

Stop after the experiment and wait for approval.

+# Phase 4 controlled overlap-confidence experiment
+
+The question is whether confidence adjustment for small co-rating overlap changes reliability and held-out retrieval. The application remains at its Phase 2 **co-rated-only raw cosine** baseline. Phase 4 changes similarity only inside an isolated analysis script:
+
+```text
+adjusted_similarity = raw_co_rated_cosine * min(co_rated_count / T, 1)
+```
+
+The primary setting is `T=10`. `T=5` and `T=20` are sensitivity checks, reported whether or not they outperform the primary setting. The factor is a confidence adjustment to the similarity estimate. It adds no rating, fills no missing matrix cell, and does not solve cold start.
+
+Run from the repository root with Node 18+:
+
+```sh
+node week03/collaborative-filtering-movie-recommender/analysis/phase4.mjs verify
+node week03/collaborative-filtering-movie-recommender/analysis/phase4.mjs evaluate
+node week03/collaborative-filtering-movie-recommender/analysis/phase4.mjs benchmark
+```
+
+These modes write only new `phase4_*.json` files under `results/`. `verify` writes full-matrix user 2 Top-5 and contributor details for raw/T5/T10/T20. `evaluate` writes all per-user holdout results and cohort support aggregates. `benchmark` measures raw versus T10 complete recommendation calls.
+
+## Holdout and validation
+
+The cohort and target selection are identical to Phase 3: 911 users with at least 21 original ratings and at least one rating `>=4`; the latest such rating by timestamp is held out, with smaller movie ID breaking timestamp ties. The held-out matrix cell is zero during scoring and restored in `finally`. The corresponding entry is also excluded from the analysis-only sparse row and column. Other users' ratings of the target movie remain available. Top-5 is sorted by descending score and ascending movie ID on exact ties; the User-Based top-20 neighborhood is sorted by descending similarity and ascending user ID. Hits compare movie IDs, not potentially duplicate titles. All users remain in the HitRate and MRR denominators even if a method returns fewer than five items.
+
+For speed, the evaluator intersects sorted observed ratings rather than scanning dense zero-filled vectors. Co-rated dot products and norms are accumulated in the same coordinate order as the application. Raw cosine is calculated once per user/user or item/item pair for a held-out user, then the four settings reuse it without carrying pair values across different holdouts. Predictions otherwise use the application's existing weighted-average formulas. The script checks the Top-5 IDs and scores from the actual application functions on held-out users 2, 65, and 405 for all four settings. For **all 911 users**, it checks raw holdout IDs, Top-5 ranks, and result counts against the saved Phase 3 baseline. It reconstructs every Top-5 prediction from the recorded contributors and checks that the full matrix and dataset hashes are restored.
+
+## Support statistics
+
+Support is measured over positive similarities that contribute to **Top-5 predictions in the held-out cohort**. A pair may contribute to more than one recommendation; each contribution is counted in the overlap distribution. Prediction support count is the number of neighbors who rated a candidate (User-Based) or active-user-rated items with positive similarity to it (Item-Based). The similarity-weight sum is the denominator of that recommendation's weighted average. Reporting median co-rated count and the fractions at `<=1`, `<=2`, and `<=5` makes the confidence change visible without changing the algorithm or selecting a threshold from the results.
+
+## Timing
+
+The fixed benchmark users are `[2, 3, 1, 405, 943]`, as in Phase 3. For each method and user, raw and T10 each receive two warmups and five measured calls. The measured order alternates raw/T10 and T10/raw to reduce ordering and JIT drift. Timing includes full on-demand recommendation calls, including item-column construction and candidate sorting. All timings are machine- and implementation-specific. They do not establish general scalability.
+
+## Interpretation boundary
+
+This is one positive holdout per eligible user, not a randomized test split or a test of all possible relevant movies. There are no observed negatives for every unchosen movie. A change of one or two Top-5 hits among 911 users is a small protocol-specific observation. The sensitivity settings are not a search for a winner, and the primary `T=10` setting is not chosen using held-out outcomes. Raw co-rated cosine is mathematically valid; small overlap can make its apparent certainty misleading. No business outcome or cold-start improvement is inferred from these results.

Hits compare movie IDs, not potentially duplicate titles. All users remain in the HitRate and MRR denominators even if a method returns fewer than five items.

For speed, the evaluator intersects sorted observed ratings rather than scanning dense zero-filled vectors. Co-rated dot products and norms are accumulated in the same coordinate order as the application. Raw cosine is calculated once per user/user or item/item pair for a held-out user, then the four settings reuse it without carrying pair values across different holdouts. Predictions otherwise use the application's existing weighted-average formulas. The script checks the Top-5 IDs and scores from the actual application functions on held-out users 2, 65, and 405 for all four settings. For **all 911 users**, it checks raw holdout IDs, Top-5 ranks, and result counts against the saved Phase 3 baseline. It reconstructs every Top-5 prediction from the recorded contributors and checks that the full matrix and dataset hashes are restored.

## Support statistics

Support is measured over positive similarities that contribute to **Top-5 predictions in the held-out cohort**. A pair may contribute to more than one recommendation; each contribution is counted in the overlap distribution. Prediction support count is the number of neighbors who rated a candidate (User-Based) or active-user-rated items with positive similarity to it (Item-Based). The similarity-weight sum is the denominator of that recommendation's weighted average. Reporting median co-rated count and the fractions at `<=1`, `<=2`, and `<=5` makes the confidence change visible without changing the algorithm or selecting a threshold from the results.

## Timing

The fixed benchmark users are `[2, 3, 1, 405, 943]`, as in Phase 3. For each method and user, raw and T10 each receive two warmups and five measured calls. The measured order alternates raw/T10 and T10/raw to reduce ordering and JIT drift. Timing includes full on-demand recommendation calls, including item-column construction and candidate sorting. All timings are machine- and implementation-specific. They do not establish general scalability.

## Interpretation boundary

This is one positive holdout per eligible user, not a randomized test split or a test of all possible relevant movies. There are no observed negatives for every unchosen movie. A change of one or two Top-5 hits among 911 users is a small protocol-specific observation. The sensitivity settings are not a search for a winner, and the primary `T=10` setting is not chosen using held-out outcomes. Raw co-rated cosine is mathematically valid; small overlap can make its apparent certainty misleading. No business outcome or cold-start improvement is inferred from these results.

content.text:
Phase 4 is complete as an isolated experiment. The application still uses raw co-rated cosine; the experimental method in [phase4.mjs](/Users/chenfengru/LLM4Rec-Course-codex/week03/collaborative-filtering-movie-recommender/analysis/phase4.mjs) applies \(s\min(n/T,1)\) during analysis only. This factor adjusts confidence in a similarity estimate; it adds no rating and imputes no missing value. The teacher baseline, datasets, UI, and Phase 3 outputs are unchanged. Nothing was committed or pushed.

**The same 911-user leave-one-out protocol** was run for raw cosine and all three thresholds. Each setting returned five recommendations for every evaluated user.

| Method | Top-5 hits | HitRate@5 | MRR@5 | Fewer than 5 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| User-Based raw | 9 | 0.988% | 0.004848 | 0 |
| User-Based T=5 | 11 | 1.207% | 0.005562 | 0 |
| **User-Based T=10** | **10** | **1.098%** | **0.004958** | **0** |
| User-Based T=20 | 5 | 0.549% | 0.002506 | 0 |
| Item-Based raw | 0 | 0% | 0 | 0 |
| Item-Based T=5 | 0 | 0% | 0 | 0 |
| **Item-Based T=10** | **0** | **0%** | **0** | **0** |
| Item-Based T=20 | 0 | 0% | 0 | 0 |

These results are in [phase4_evaluation.json](/Users/chenfengru/LLM4Rec-Course-codex/week03/collaborative-filtering-movie-recommender/results/phase4_evaluation.json). Every raw per-user hit, rank, and result count matched Phase 3. The analysis scores were also checked against the application functions on held-out users for all four settings.

**T=10 substantially changed the evidence behind User-Based Top-5 predictions, but barely changed Item-Based support.** The table counts positive similarities contributing to Top-5 predictions across the held-out cohort; a pair contributing to two predictions is counted twice.

| Method | Median co-rated count | Contributions with ≤1 / ≤2 / ≤5 co-ratings | Mean contributors per prediction | Mean similarity-weight sum |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: |
| User-Based raw | 1 | 54.2% / 71.1% / 85.1% | 1.26 | 1.25 |
| User-Based T=10 | 14 | 0% / 0% / 0% | 1.61 | 1.57 |
| Item-Based raw | 1 | 95.8% / 98.8% / 99.8% | 20.21 | 20.14 |
| Item-Based T=10 | 1 | 91.7% / 97.3% / 99.7% | 21.40 | 2.40 |

The median **prediction support count** remained 1 for User-Based and 9 for Item-Based in both settings. Weight sums are denominators after applying the chosen similarity, so their raw and adjusted values have different scales.

For **user 2**, T=10 replaced all five User-Based titles. Raw Top-5 contributing similarities rested on **1–4** shared movies; the T=10 list’s contributors rested on **11–21**. The new list includes *Paths of Glory*, *Taxi Driver*, *Priest*, *Wallace & Gromit*, and *Return of the Pink Panther*. All five scores still display as **5.000**, because their contributing neighbors rated those candidates 5. The number of contributors per movie did not uniformly increase: the raw list used **2, 3, 2, 1, 1**, while T=10 used **2, 2, 1, 1, 1**.

User 2’s Item-Based list kept the **same five movies**, swapping the first two positions. Scores and contributor counts stayed the same. Every underlying item similarity still had **one** co-rating; T=10 multiplied every such weight by 0.1, which cancels in a normalized weighted average. Full before/after titles, scores, weights, and contributors are in [phase4_user2.json](/Users/chenfengru/LLM4Rec-Course-codex/week03/collaborative-filtering-movie-recommender/results/phase4_user2.json).

The paired runtime benchmark used Phase 3’s five fixed users, two warmups, and five measured calls per user and method. It alternated raw and T=10 call order.

| Complete recommendation call | Raw mean / median | T=10 mean / median |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| User-Based | 1.58 / 1.38 ms | 1.73 / 1.65 ms |
| Item-Based | 290 / 247 ms | 361 / 304 ms |

On these calls, T=10 was slower by about **9%** in mean User-Based time and **24%** in mean Item-Based time. These are measurements of this JavaScript implementation on this machine, not general scalability estimates. Per-user timings are in [phase4_efficiency.json](/Users/chenfengru/LLM4Rec-Course-codex/week03/collaborative-filtering-movie-recommender/results/phase4_efficiency.json).

**The hypothesis is supported for User-Based overlap support, but not as a stable recommendation-quality improvement across settings or as an Item-Based remedy.** At T=10, User-Based gained 10 held-out hits and lost 9 raw-cosine hits: a net gain of one user. T=5 gained two net hits; T=20 lost four. Item-Based gained none. Raw cosine is mathematically valid, while a high value from very small overlap can carry little evidence. This adjustment does not solve cold start.

The [reproduction protocol](/Users/chenfengru/LLM4Rec-Course-codex/week03/collaborative-filtering-movie-recommender/analysis/phase4_protocol.md) records the holdout, tie-breaking, validation, and timing details. What remains unresolved is performance under other evaluation splits, whether the single-positive Top-5 test reflects broader relevance, and how to address Item-Based rankings dominated by one-overlap similarities. I’ve stopped before changing the baseline or choosing a threshold for the application.

Nothing was committed or pushed.

**The same 911-user leave-one-out protocol** was run for raw cosine and all three thresholds. Each setting returned five recommendations for every evaluated user.

| Method | Top-5 hits | HitRate@5 | MRR@5 | Fewer than 5 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| User-Based raw | 9 | 0.988% | 0.004848 | 0 |
| User-Based T=5 | 11 | 1.207% | 0.005562 | 0 |
| **User-Based T=10** | **10** | **1.098%** | **0.004958** | **0** |
| User-Based T=20 | 5 | 0.549% | 0.002506 | 0 |
| Item-Based raw | 0 | 0% | 0 | 0 |
| Item-Based T=5 | 0 | 0% | 0 | 0 |
| **Item-Based T=10** | **0** | **0%** | **0** | **0** |
| Item-Based T=20 | 0 | 0% | 0 | 0 |

These results are in [phase4_evaluation.json](/Users/chenfengru/LLM4Rec-Course-codex/week03/collaborative-filtering-movie-recommender/results/phase4_evaluation.json). Every raw per-user hit, rank, and result count matched Phase 3. The analysis scores were also checked against the application functions on held-out users for all four settings.

**T=10 substantially changed the evidence behind User-Based Top-5 predictions, but barely changed Item-Based support.** The table counts positive similarities contributing to Top-5 predictions across the held-out cohort; a pair contributing to two predictions is counted twice.

| Method | Median co-rated count | Contributions with ≤1 / ≤2 / ≤5 co-ratings | Mean contributors per prediction | Mean similarity-weight sum |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: |
| User-Based raw | 1 | 54.2% / 71.1% / 85.1% | 1.26 | 1.25 |
| User-Based T=10 | 14 | 0% / 0% / 0% | 1.61 | 1.57 |
| Item-Based raw | 1 | 95.8% / 98.8% / 99.8% | 20.21 | 20.14 |
| Item-Based T=10 | 1 | 91.7% / 97.3% / 99.7% | 21.40 | 2.40 |

The median **prediction support count** remained 1 for User-Based and 9 for Item-Based in both settings. Weight sums are denominators after applying the chosen similarity, so their raw and adjusted values have different scales.

For **user 2**, T=10 replaced all five User-Based titles. Raw Top-5 contributing similarities rested on **1–4** shared movies; the T=10 list’s contributors rested on **11–21**. The new list includes *Paths of Glory*, *Taxi Driver*, *Priest*, *Wallace & Gromit*, and *Return of the Pink Panther*. All five scores still display as **5.000**, because their contributing neighbors rated those candidates 5. The number of contributors per movie did not uniformly increase: the raw list used **2, 3, 2, 1, 1**, while T=10 used **2, 2, 1, 1, 1**.

User 2’s Item-Based list kept the **same five movies**, swapping the first two positions. Scores and contributor counts stayed the same. Every underlying item similarity still had **one** co-rating; T=10 multiplied every such weight by 0.1, which cancels in a normalized weighted average. Full before/after titles, scores, weights, and contributors are in [phase4_user2.json](/Users/chenfengru/LLM4Rec-Course-codex/week03/collaborative-filtering-movie-recommender/results/phase4_user2.json).

The paired runtime benchmark used Phase 3’s five fixed users, two warmups, and five measured calls per user and method. It alternated raw and T=10 call order.

| Complete recommendation call | Raw mean / median | T=10 mean / median |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| User-Based | 1.58 / 1.38 ms | 1.73 / 1.65 ms |
| Item-Based | 290 / 247 ms | 361 / 304 ms |

On these calls, T=10 was slower by about **9%** in mean User-Based time and **24%** in mean Item-Based time. These are measurements of this JavaScript implementation on this machine, not general scalability estimates. Per-user timings are in [phase4_efficiency.json](/Users/chenfengru/LLM4Rec-Course-codex/week03/collaborative-filtering-movie-recommender/results/phase4_efficiency.json).

**The hypothesis is supported for User-Based overlap support, but not as a stable recommendation-quality improvement across settings or as an Item-Based remedy.** At T=10, User-Based gained 10 held-out hits and lost 9 raw-cosine hits: a net gain of one user. T=5 gained two net hits; T=20 lost four. Item-Based gained none. Raw cosine is mathematically valid, while a high value from very small overlap can carry little evidence. This adjustment does not solve cold start.

The [reproduction protocol](/Users/chenfengru/LLM4Rec-Course-codex/week03/collaborative-filtering-movie-recommender/analysis/phase4_protocol.md) records the holdout, tie-breaking, validation, and timing details. What remains unresolved is performance under other evaluation splits, whether the single-positive Top-5 test reflects broader relevance, and how to address Item-Based rankings dominated by one-overlap similarities. I’ve stopped before changing the baseline or choosing a threshold for the application.

Phase 4 is accepted.

Decision:
Do NOT replace the application baseline with overlap weighting.

Keep the final application implementation as raw co-rated-only cosine.

Treat overlap weighting as a controlled improvement experiment:
it improved User-Based similarity support substantially, but recommendation
quality gains were small and threshold-sensitive, and it did not solve the
Item-Based failure mode.

Now perform Phase 5: Week 2 vs Week 3 comparison and final evidence synthesis.

Do not modify week03/teacher-baseline/.
Do not modify datasets.
Do not commit or push.
Do not tune additional overlap thresholds.
Do not change the CF algorithms.

1. Align Week 2 and Week 3 evaluation

Use the existing Week 3 leave-one-out cohort/protocol where possible.

For each eligible user:

- use the same held-out positive movie from Phase 3;
- ensure the held-out movie is unavailable to the Week 3 recommender;
- construct an appropriate Week 2 content-based query using only information
  that would have been available before the held-out item.

Prefer the Week 2 three-movie profile method if it can be aligned cleanly.
Use the user's most recent positive movies BEFORE the held-out interaction,
not the held-out item itself.

Exclude the user's already-seen movies consistently.

Document any users who cannot be aligned.

2. Compare three methods

A. Week 2 content-based profile Top-5
B. Week 3 User-Based CF Top-5
C. Week 3 Item-Based CF Top-5

For each method report:

- evaluated users,
- HitRate\@5,
- MRR\@5,
- fewer-than-5 result count.

Also measure pairwise Top-5 set overlap:

- Content-Based vs User-Based,
- Content-Based vs Item-Based,
- User-Based vs Item-Based.

Report mean shared items out of 5 and fraction of users with zero overlap.

Do NOT compare raw cosine scores with predicted ratings directly.

3. Case studies

Choose 2–3 representative users:

- one where Content-Based succeeds and CF fails,
- one where User-Based succeeds and Content-Based fails, if such a case exists,
- one illustrative failure case for Item-Based.

For each, show:

- input history/profile,
- held-out movie,
- three Top-5 lists,
- why the methods differ.

Ground explanations in:

- genre similarity for Week 2,
- user-rating behavior for User-Based CF,
- item co-rating behavior for Item-Based CF.

Do not infer business relevance from movie titles alone.

4. Final Week 3 evidence table

Create a concise machine-readable and Markdown summary containing:

Implementation:

- 943 users
- 1682 movies
- 100000 ratings
- raw co-rated-only cosine
- User-Based top 20 neighbors
- Top-5 outputs

Reliability:

- user-pair median overlap
- item-pair median overlap
- <=2 overlap fractions
- high-cosine low-support fractions

Evaluation:

- raw User-Based HitRate\@5 / MRR\@5
- raw Item-Based HitRate\@5 / MRR\@5
- overlap-weighting sensitivity results

Efficiency:

- theoretical user-user vs item-item pair counts
- measured on-demand runtimes

Week 2 vs Week 3:

- aligned evaluation results
- Top-5 overlap statistics.

5. Check required homework questions

Explicitly map the collected evidence to:

A. User-Based vs Item-Based quality and efficiency.
B. Missing-value strategy trade-off:
co-rated-only vs mean imputation vs weighted approach vs matrix factorization.
For alternatives not implemented, discuss conceptually from the course
material; do not invent empirical results.
C. Cold start and sparsity.
D. Week 2 content-based vs Week 3 collaborative filtering.

Mark any part that still lacks evidence.

6. Scope

Do not write report.pdf yet.
Do not alter the main application unless a genuine implementation defect
is discovered.
Do not claim that overlap weighting is the final method.

Save outputs under analysis/ and results/.

At the end report:
A. aligned Week 2 vs Week 3 metrics,
B. Top-5 overlap statistics,
C. representative cases,
D. final evidence table,
E. coverage of all homework questions,
F. anything still missing before report writing.

Stop and wait for approval.

# Week 3 final evidence

The final application uses **raw co-rated-only cosine**. Phase 4 overlap confidence is an analysis-only experiment. Scores from Week 2 genre cosine and Week 3 predicted ratings are not directly comparable.

## Implementation and reliability

| Item | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Users / movies / ratings | 943 / 1,682 / 100,000 |
| Rating and missing convention | Observed 1–5; zero internally means unrated |
| Final similarity | Raw co-rated-only cosine; zero for no overlap or zero norm |
| User-Based neighborhood / output | Up to 20 positive neighbors / Top-5 |
| Median co-rated count, user / item pairs | 10 / 1 |
| Pair fraction with ≤2 co-ratings, user / item | 14.29% / 60.38% |
| High-cosine (≥0.9) pairs with ≤2 co-ratings, user / item | 11.94% / 47.70% |

The pair counts are 444,153 unique user pairs and 1,413,721 unique item pairs. Small overlap does not make cosine mathematically incorrect; it limits how much evidence supports that value.

## Held-out evaluation

Phase 3 used 911 users, each with the most recent rating ≥4 held out and at least 20 remaining ratings.

| Method | Hits | HitRate@5 | MRR@5 | Fewer than five |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Raw User-Based | 9 | 0.99% | 0.005 | 0 |
| Raw Item-Based | 0 | 0.00% | 0.000 | 0 |

The controlled overlap-confidence experiment used the same 911 users. T=10 was primary; T=5 and T=20 were sensitivity checks.

| Setting | User hits / HR@5 / MRR@5 | Item hits / HR@5 / MRR@5 | Median contributing overlap, user / item |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| T5 | 11 / 1.21% / 0.006 | 0 / 0.00% / 0.000 | 7 / 1 |
| T10 | 10 / 1.10% / 0.005 | 0 / 0.00% / 0.000 | 14 / 1 |
| T20 | 5 / 0.55% / 0.003 | 0 / 0.00% / 0.000 | 25 / 1 |

The T=10 User-Based gain was one net hit (10 gained, 9 lost relative to raw), and T=20 fell below raw. Item-Based remained at zero. No weighted setting was adopted in the application.

## Efficiency

| Dimension | Full square including self | Unique unordered excluding self |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Users | 889,249 | 444,153 |
| Items | 2,829,124 | 1,413,721 |

Phase 3 timed complete raw on-demand calls on users [2, 3, 1, 405, 943], with two warmups and five measured calls each: User-Based mean/median 1.588/1.398 ms; Item-Based 388.484/332.312 ms. Full pair counts and on-demand runtimes answer different questions; neither predicts general scalability.

## Aligned Week 2 versus Week 3

The 853-user primary comparison reuses Phase 3 held-out targets. It requires at least 20 user ratings and three positive profile movies with timestamps strictly earlier than the target. Of the 911 Phase 3 users, 57 lack 20 earlier ratings and one further user lacks three earlier positives. The same earlier-only active-user row and unseen-movie candidate pool are used for all methods. Other users retain full histories; this is not a global chronological split.

| Method | Users | Hits | HitRate@5 | MRR@5 | Fewer than five |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Week 2 three-movie binary-genre profile | 853 | 20 | 2.34% | 0.010 | 0 |
| Week 3 User-Based raw | 853 | 12 | 1.41% | 0.008 | 0 |
| Week 3 Item-Based raw | 853 | 0 | 0.00% | 0.000 | 0 |

| Top-5 pair | Mean shared movies out of 5 | Users with zero overlap |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Content / User-Based | 0.081 | 785/853 (92.03%) |
| Content / Item-Based | 0.001 | 852/853 (99.88%) |
| User-Based / Item-Based | 0.000 | 853/853 (100.00%) |

Low list overlap describes different rankings; it does not establish which list is more relevant. The 853-user results should not be substituted for Phase 3's 911-user results because the active-user history was restricted to earlier interactions.

## Representative cases

### User 79: contentSucceedsCfFails

Earlier ratings: 53. Profile: I Shot Andy Warhol (1996) (4/5); Star Trek: First Contact (1996) (4/5); Shanghai Triad (Yao a yao yao dao waipo qiao) (1995) (4/5). Held-out: Twelve Monkeys (1995) (5/5).

| Rank | Week 2 profile | Week 3 User-Based | Week 3 Item-Based |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Ben-Hur (1959) | Usual Suspects, The (1995) | King of New York (1990) |
| 2 | Twelve Monkeys (1995) | From Dusk Till Dawn (1996) | Mamma Roma (1962) |
| 3 | Mad City (1997) | Braveheart (1995) | Police Story 4: Project S (Chao ji ji hua) (1993) |
| 4 | Day the Earth Stood Still, The (1951) | Birdcage, The (1996) | Fire on the Mountain (1996) |
| 5 | Perfect World, A (1993) | Brothers McMullen, The (1995) | Daniel Defoe's Robinson Crusoe (1996) |

The held-out movie has Drama and Sci-Fi tags. Drama appears in two profile movies and Sci-Fi in one, giving Week 2 a genre cosine of 0.802 and rank 2. User-Based predicts 3.2 from five contributing neighbors while its Top-5 scores are 5; Item-Based predicts 4.021 for the held-out movie while its Top-5 scores are at least 4.313. This explains the list difference through observed features and ratings.

### User 20: userCfSucceedsContentFails

Earlier ratings: 45. Profile: Jurassic Park (1993) (4/5); Lost World: Jurassic Park, The (1997) (4/5); Braveheart (1995) (5/5). Held-out: Searching for Bobby Fischer (1993) (5/5).

| Rank | Week 2 profile | Week 3 User-Based | Week 3 Item-Based |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Stargate (1994) | Shanghai Triad (Yao a yao yao dao waipo qiao) (1995) | Coldblooded (1995) |
| 2 | Star Trek: First Contact (1996) | Dead Man Walking (1995) | Rough Magic (1995) |
| 3 | Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country (1991) | Postino, Il (1994) | Turning, The (1992) |
| 4 | Star Trek: The Wrath of Khan (1982) | Crumb (1994) | Ill Gotten Gains (1997) |
| 5 | Star Trek III: The Search for Spock (1984) | Searching for Bobby Fischer (1993) | Intimate Relations (1996) |

The profile is dominated by Action, Adventure, and Sci-Fi; the held-out movie is Drama only, with genre cosine 0.224. User-Based ranks it fifth at a predicted 5, but that prediction is from one neighbor whose similarity rests on one shared rating. The hit is real under the protocol and has weak support. Item-Based gives the target 3.091, below its Top-5 cutoff.

### User 2: itemCfFailure

Earlier ratings: 57. Profile: Air Force One (1997) (4/5); Fly Away Home (1996) (4/5); Good Will Hunting (1997) (5/5). Held-out: As Good As It Gets (1997) (5/5).

| Rank | Week 2 profile | Week 3 User-Based | Week 3 Item-Based |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | GoldenEye (1995) | Maltese Falcon, The (1941) | They Made Me a Criminal (1939) |
| 2 | Apollo 13 (1995) | It Happened One Night (1934) | Shadows (Cienie) (1988) |
| 3 | Free Willy 2: The Adventure Home (1995) | Manchurian Candidate, The (1962) | The Courtyard (1995) |
| 4 | Outbreak (1995) | Babe (1995) | Yankee Zulu (1994) |
| 5 | Free Willy (1993) | From Dusk Till Dawn (1996) | Hostile Intentions (1994) |

The held-out Comedy/Drama movie has genre cosine 0.316 against the three-movie profile. User-Based predicts 5 from one neighbor but does not rank it in Top-5. Item-Based predicts 3.807 from 57 positive item similarities; its Top-5 instead scores 4.5 for movies with only one observed rating each. Those winning similarities have one co-rating. This is a concrete sparse-item ranking failure under the protocol.

## Homework question coverage and remaining evidence

- **A. User-Based versus Item-Based quality and efficiency:** measured both held-out retrieval and local on-demand runtime. In these protocols User-Based hit more targets and ran faster. The dataset has more items than users, so a full item-pair matrix also has more pairs. These observations do not establish general superiority.
- **B. Missing-value strategies:** co-rated-only uses only observed data and is simple, but the measured overlap distributions show unreliable-looking high similarities from few shared ratings. Overlap-confidence weighting was measured: it improved User-Based support, had small threshold-sensitive hit changes, and did not resolve Item-Based's zero hits. **Mean imputation** could provide dense vectors but can introduce average-rating bias and must preserve the original observed mask; **matrix factorization** could learn latent representations from sparse data but needs training, validation, and more computation. The latter two were not implemented or empirically compared.
- **C. Cold start and sparsity:** without a rated item, a new user has no co-rated entries for User-Based similarity and no rated items to seed Item-Based scores. An unrated new movie also lacks item co-ratings. The observed MovieLens sparsity and low-overlap statistics support the reliability concern; the dataset has no zero-history users for an empirical cold-start test. Confidence weighting does not create new interactions.
- **D. Week 2 versus Week 3:** the aligned 853-user outcomes and pairwise list overlaps are measured. Week 2 uses genre similarity from three earlier liked movies; Week 3 uses ratings from the earlier active-user history and other users. Raw score scales differ, and the comparison retains other users' full histories.

Further evidence before a broad quality or business claim would require additional held-out targets or splits, a global time-aware protocol if temporal causality matters, and direct tests of cold-start handling or alternative algorithms. No user or business outcomes were measured.

Sources: machine-readable files in ../results/phase3_*, ../results/phase4_evaluation.json, ../results/phase5_aligned_comparison.json, and ../results/phase5_cases.json.

The final application uses **raw co-rated-only cosine**. Phase 4 overlap confidence is an analysis-only experiment. Scores from Week 2 genre cosine and Week 3 predicted ratings are not directly comparable.

## Implementation and reliability

| Item | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Users / movies / ratings | 943 / 1,682 / 100,000 |
| Rating and missing convention | Observed 1–5; zero internally means unrated |

Phase 3 used 911 users, each with the most recent rating ≥4 held out and at least 20 remaining ratings.

We are starting Week 3 of my LLM4Rec course.

Repository root:
/Users/chenfengru/LLM4Rec-Course-codex

Current branch must be:
week03-collaborative-filtering

The instructor's untouched Week 3 starter code is in:
week03/teacher-baseline/

Important rules:

1. Do NOT modify anything under week03/teacher-baseline/.
2. First verify the current branch and git status.
3. Create my working directory:
   week03/collaborative-filtering-movie-recommender/
   by copying the instructor baseline exactly.
4. Verify that the copied starter files initially match the baseline.
5. Do NOT implement the homework yet.
6. Audit the full Week 3 starter code and specification before making any functional changes.

Please inspect at least:

- week03/teacher-baseline/readme.md
- data.js
- script.js
- index.html
- style.css
- u.data / u.item structure where relevant

The goal of this first pass is to understand the starter implementation and look for any seeded or semantic defect, similar to the Week 2 genre-index problem.

For every suspected issue:

- show the exact file and relevant code,
- explain the observed behavior,
- distinguish symptom from root cause,
- give a concrete way to verify whether it is actually a defect,
- do not fix it yet unless verification is required to prove the issue.

Also summarize:
A. what the current starter application already implements,
B. what the Week 3 assignment still requires,
C. what missing-value strategy the starter currently uses,
D. how User-Based CF and Item-Based CF are currently implemented,
E. any mismatch between readme/specification and actual code,
F. the most important things we should manually verify before editing.

Do not assume a bug exists just because one is expected.
Investigate first and report evidence.

Stop after the audit and wait for my approval before implementing changes.

We have completed the Week 3 starter audit.

Now proceed with Phase 2 implementation in:

week03/collaborative-filtering-movie-recommender/

Do NOT modify:
week03/teacher-baseline/

Use the following decisions.

1. Missing-value strategy
   Use CO-RATED ITEMS ONLY consistently.

For any cosine similarity:

- ignore entries where either side is unrated,
- do not impute missing values,
- return 0 if there are no co-rated entries or the denominator is zero.

Add a clear comment near the similarity function documenting this choice.

2. First fix the confirmed MovieLens genre-index bug
   The 19 MovieLens genre flags include "unknown" first.
   Add the missing "unknown" genre label so all 19 flags align correctly.

Add a minimal regression verification:

- Toy Story (movie 1) must be exactly:
  Animation, Children's, Comedy
- Western-tagged movies must remain reachable.

Do not change the dataset files.

3. Implement the rating matrix

Build:
ratingMatrix[userId][movieId]

Use 0 only as the internal marker for "unrated".
Actual MovieLens ratings are 1–5.

Verify:

- 943 users
- 1682 movies
- 100000 observed ratings

4. Implement cosineSimilarity(a, b)

Use only co-rated, non-zero entries.

Also expose or record the co-rated count for diagnostic/testing purposes if this can be done cleanly without complicating the public API.

5. Implement User-Based CF

For active user u:

- compute cosine similarity to every other user,

- keep only positive-similarity neighbors,

- choose up to the top 20 neighbors,

- for each movie not rated by u, predict:

  predicted\_score =
  sum(sim(u,v) \* rating(v,i))
  /
  sum(sim(u,v))

  using only neighbors who rated movie i.

- skip a candidate if the denominator is zero,

- sort descending,

- return Top-5.

Never recommend a movie already rated by the active user.

6. Implement Item-Based CF

For each unseen candidate movie i:

- compare its rating column against movies j already rated by the active user,

- use the same co-rated-only cosine strategy,

- compute:

  predicted\_score =
  sum(sim(i,j) \* rating(u,j))
  /
  sum(sim(i,j))

- use only positive similarities,

- skip candidates with zero denominator,

- sort descending,

- return Top-5.

Never recommend a movie already rated by the active user.

7. Verification before UI conclusions

Create small deterministic tests/analysis scripts outside teacher-baseline.

At minimum verify:

A. cosine on a tiny manually-checkable matrix,
B. identical vectors give cosine 1,
C. no overlap gives cosine 0,
D. a single shared rating can mathematically give cosine 1,

- keep only positive-similarity neighbors,

- choose up to the top 20 neighbors,

- for each movie not rated by u, predict:

  predicted\_score =
  sum(sim(u,v) \* rating(v,i))
  /
  sum(sim(u,v))

  using only neighbors who rated movie i.

- skip a candidate if the denominator is zero,

- sort descending,

- return Top-5.

Never recommend a movie already rated by the active user.

For each unseen candidate movie i:

- compare its rating column against movies j already rated by the active user,

- use the same co-rated-only cosine strategy,

- compute:

  predicted\_score =
  sum(sim(i,j) \* rating(u,j))
  /
  sum(sim(i,j))

- use only positive similarities,

- skip candidates with zero denominator,

- sort descending,

week03/collaborative-filtering-movie-recommender/analysis/

content.text:
Phase 4 is complete as an isolated experiment. The application still uses raw co-rated cosine; the experimental method in [phase4.mjs](/Users/chenfengru/LLM4Rec-Course-codex/week03/collaborative-filtering-movie-recommender/analysis/phase4.mjs) applies \(s\min(n/T,1)\) during analysis only. This factor adjusts confidence in a similarity estimate; it adds no rating and imputes no missing value. The teacher baseline, datasets, UI, and Phase 3 outputs are unchanged. Nothing was committed or pushed.

**The same 911-user leave-one-out protocol** was run for raw cosine and all three thresholds. Each setting returned five recommendations for every evaluated user.

| Method | Top-5 hits | HitRate@5 | MRR@5 | Fewer than 5 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| User-Based raw | 9 | 0.988% | 0.004848 | 0 |
| User-Based T=5 | 11 | 1.207% | 0.005562 | 0 |
| **User-Based T=10** | **10** | **1.098%** | **0.004958** | **0** |
| User-Based T=20 | 5 | 0.549% | 0.002506 | 0 |
| Item-Based raw | 0 | 0% | 0 | 0 |
| Item-Based T=5 | 0 | 0% | 0 | 0 |
| **Item-Based T=10** | **0** | **0%** | **0** | **0** |
| Item-Based T=20 | 0 | 0% | 0 | 0 |

These results are in [phase4_evaluation.json](/Users/chenfengru/LLM4Rec-Course-codex/week03/collaborative-filtering-movie-recommender/results/phase4_evaluation.json). Every raw per-user hit, rank, and result count matched Phase 3. The analysis scores were also checked against the application functions on held-out users for all four settings.

**T=10 substantially changed the evidence behind User-Based Top-5 predictions, but barely changed Item-Based support.** The table counts positive similarities contributing to Top-5 predictions across the held-out cohort; a pair contributing to two predictions is counted twice.

| Method | Median co-rated count | Contributions with ≤1 / ≤2 / ≤5 co-ratings | Mean contributors per prediction | Mean similarity-weight sum |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: |
| User-Based raw | 1 | 54.2% / 71.1% / 85.1% | 1.26 | 1.25 |
| User-Based T=10 | 14 | 0% / 0% / 0% | 1.61 | 1.57 |
| Item-Based raw | 1 | 95.8% / 98.8% / 99.8% | 20.21 | 20.14 |
| Item-Based T=10 | 1 | 91.7% / 97.3% / 99.7% | 21.40 | 2.40 |

The median **prediction support count** remained 1 for User-Based and 9 for Item-Based in both settings. Weight sums are denominators after applying the chosen similarity, so their raw and adjusted values have different scales.

For **user 2**, T=10 replaced all five User-Based titles. Raw Top-5 contributing similarities rested on **1–4** shared movies; the T=10 list’s contributors rested on **11–21**. The new list includes *Paths of Glory*, *Taxi Driver*, *Priest*, *Wallace & Gromit*, and *Return of the Pink Panther*. All five scores still display as **5.000**, because their contributing neighbors rated those candidates 5. The number of contributors per movie did not uniformly increase: the raw list used **2, 3, 2, 1, 1**, while T=10 used **2, 2, 1, 1, 1**.

User 2’s Item-Based list kept the **same five movies**, swapping the first two positions. Scores and contributor counts stayed the same. Every underlying item similarity still had **one** co-rating; T=10 multiplied every such weight by 0.1, which cancels in a normalized weighted average. Full before/after titles, scores, weights, and contributors are in [phase4_user2.json](/Users/chenfengru/LLM4Rec-Course-codex/week03/collaborative-filtering-movie-recommender/results/phase4_user2.json).

The paired runtime benchmark used Phase 3’s five fixed users, two warmups, and five measured calls per user and method. It alternated raw and T=10 call order.

| Complete recommendation call | Raw mean / median | T=10 mean / median |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| User-Based | 1.58 / 1.38 ms | 1.73 / 1.65 ms |
| Item-Based | 290 / 247 ms | 361 / 304 ms |

On these calls, T=10 was slower by about **9%** in mean User-Based time and **24%** in mean Item-Based time. These are measurements of this JavaScript implementation on this machine, not general scalability estimates. Per-user timings are in [phase4_efficiency.json](/Users/chenfengru/LLM4Rec-Course-codex/week03/collaborative-filtering-movie-recommender/results/phase4_efficiency.json).

**The hypothesis is supported for User-Based overlap support, but not as a stable recommendation-quality improvement across settings or as an Item-Based remedy.** At T=10, User-Based gained 10 held-out hits and lost 9 raw-cosine hits: a net gain of one user. T=5 gained two net hits; T=20 lost four. Item-Based gained none. Raw cosine is mathematically valid, while a high value from very small overlap can carry little evidence. This adjustment does not solve cold start.

The [reproduction protocol](/Users/chenfengru/LLM4Rec-Course-codex/week03/collaborative-filtering-movie-recommender/analysis/phase4_protocol.md) records the holdout, tie-breaking, validation, and timing details. What remains unresolved is performance under other evaluation splits, whether the single-positive Top-5 test reflects broader relevance, and how to address Item-Based rankings dominated by one-overlap similarities. I’ve stopped before changing the baseline or choosing a threshold for the application.

Phase 4 is accepted.

Decision:
Do NOT replace the application baseline with overlap weighting.

Keep the final application implementation as raw co-rated-only cosine.

Treat overlap weighting as a controlled improvement experiment:
it improved User-Based similarity support substantially, but recommendation
quality gains were small and threshold-sensitive, and it did not solve the
Item-Based failure mode.

Now perform Phase 5: Week 2 vs Week 3 comparison and final evidence synthesis.

Do not modify week03/teacher-baseline/.
Do not modify datasets.
Do not commit or push.
Do not tune additional overlap thresholds.
Do not change the CF algorithms.

1. Align Week 2 and Week 3 evaluation

Use the existing Week 3 leave-one-out cohort/protocol where possible.

For each eligible user:

- use the same held-out positive movie from Phase 3;
- ensure the held-out movie is unavailable to the Week 3 recommender;
- construct an appropriate Week 2 content-based query using only information
  that would have been available before the held-out item.

Prefer the Week 2 three-movie profile method if it can be aligned cleanly.
Use the user's most recent positive movies BEFORE the held-out interaction,
not the held-out item itself.

Exclude the user's already-seen movies consistently.

Document any users who cannot be aligned.

2. Compare three methods

A. Week 2 content-based profile Top-5
B. Week 3 User-Based CF Top-5
C. Week 3 Item-Based CF Top-5

For each method report:

- evaluated users,
- HitRate\@5,
- MRR\@5,
- fewer-than-5 result count.

Also measure pairwise Top-5 set overlap:

- Content-Based vs User-Based,
- Content-Based vs Item-Based,
- User-Based vs Item-Based.

Report mean shared items out of 5 and fraction of users with zero overlap.

Do NOT compare raw cosine scores with predicted ratings directly.

3. Case studies

Choose 2–3 representative users:

- one where Content-Based succeeds and CF fails,
- one where User-Based succeeds and Content-Based fails, if such a case exists,
- one illustrative failure case for Item-Based.

For each, show:

- input history/profile,
- held-out movie,
- three Top-5 lists,
- why the methods differ.

Ground explanations in:

- genre similarity for Week 2,
- user-rating behavior for User-Based CF,
- item co-rating behavior for Item-Based CF.

Do not infer business relevance from movie titles alone.

4. Final Week 3 evidence table

Create a concise machine-readable and Markdown summary containing:

Implementation:

- 943 users
- 1682 movies
- 100000 ratings
- raw co-rated-only cosine
- User-Based top 20 neighbors
- Top-5 outputs

Reliability:

- user-pair median overlap
- item-pair median overlap
- <=2 overlap fractions
- high-cosine low-support fractions

Evaluation:

- raw User-Based HitRate\@5 / MRR\@5
- raw Item-Based HitRate\@5 / MRR\@5
- overlap-weighting sensitivity results

Efficiency:

- theoretical user-user vs item-item pair counts
- measured on-demand runtimes

Week 2 vs Week 3:

- aligned evaluation results
- Top-5 overlap statistics.

5. Check required homework questions

Explicitly map the collected evidence to:

A. User-Based vs Item-Based quality and efficiency.
B. Missing-value strategy trade-off:
co-rated-only vs mean imputation vs weighted approach vs matrix factorization.
For alternatives not implemented, discuss conceptually from the course
material; do not invent empirical results.
C. Cold start and sparsity.
D. Week 2 content-based vs Week 3 collaborative filtering.

Mark any part that still lacks evidence.

6. Scope

Do not write report.pdf yet.
Do not alter the main application unless a genuine implementation defect
is discovered.
Do not claim that overlap weighting is the final method.

Save outputs under analysis/ and results/.

At the end report:
A. aligned Week 2 vs Week 3 metrics,
B. Top-5 overlap statistics,
C. representative cases,
D. final evidence table,
E. coverage of all homework questions,
F. anything still missing before report writing.

Stop and wait for approval.

I’ll build the comparison from the Week 3 holdout records and Week 2’s existing binary-genre profile code. I’ll first count users with three positive movies strictly before the held-out timestamp, then choose an evaluation state that keeps the held-out item and later user history out of the comparison. I’ll document how that state relates to the Phase 3 results.

| 4 | Star Trek: The Wrath of Khan (1982) | Crumb (1994) | Ill Gotten Gains (1997) |
| 5 | Star Trek III: The Search for Spock (1984) | Searching for Bobby Fischer (1993) | Intimate Relations (1996) |

The profile is dominated by Action, Adventure, and Sci-Fi; the held-out movie is Drama only, with genre cosine 0.224. User-Based ranks it fifth at a predicted 5, but that prediction is from one neighbor whose similarity rests on one shared rating. The hit is real under the protocol and has weak support. Item-Based gives the target 3.091, below its Top-5 cutoff.

### User 2: itemCfFailure

Earlier ratings: 57. Profile: Air Force One (1997) (4/5); Fly Away Home (1996) (4/5); Good Will Hunting (1997) (5/5). Held-out: As Good As It Gets (1997) (5/5).

| Rank | Week 2 profile | Week 3 User-Based | Week 3 Item-Based |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | GoldenEye (1995) | Maltese Falcon, The (1941) | They Made Me a Criminal (1939) |
| 2 | Apollo 13 (1995) | It Happened One Night (1934) | Shadows (Cienie) (1988) |
| 3 | Free Willy 2: The Adventure Home (1995) | Manchurian Candidate, The (1962) | The Courtyard (1995) |
| 4 | Outbreak (1995) | Babe (1995) | Yankee Zulu (1994) |
| 5 | Free Willy (1993) | From Dusk Till Dawn (1996) | Hostile Intentions (1994) |

The held-out Comedy/Drama movie has genre cosine 0.316 against the three-movie profile. User-Based predicts 5 from one neighbor but does not rank it in Top-5. Item-Based predicts 3.807 from 57 positive item similarities; its Top-5 instead scores 4.5 for movies with only one observed rating each. Those winning similarities have one co-rating. This is a concrete sparse-item ranking failure under the protocol.

## Homework question coverage and remaining evidence

- **A. User-Based versus Item-Based quality and efficiency:** measured both held-out retrieval and local on-demand runtime. In these protocols User-Based hit more targets and ran faster. The dataset has more items than users, so a full item-pair matrix also has more pairs. These observations do not establish general superiority.
- **B. Missing-value strategies:** co-rated-only uses only observed data and is simple, but the measured overlap distributions show unreliable-looking high similarities from few shared ratings. Overlap-confidence weighting was measured: it improved User-Based support, had small threshold-sensitive hit changes, and did not resolve Item-Based's zero hits. **Mean imputation** could provide dense vectors but can introduce average-rating bias and must preserve the original observed mask; **matrix factorization** could learn latent representations from sparse data but needs training, validation, and more computation. The latter two were not implemented or empirically compared.
- **C. Cold start and sparsity:** without a rated item, a new user has no co-rated entries for User-Based similarity and no rated items to seed Item-Based scores. An unrated new movie also lacks item co-ratings. The observed MovieLens sparsity and low-overlap statistics support the reliability concern; the dataset has no zero-history users for an empirical cold-start test. Confidence weighting does not create new interactions.
- **D. Week 2 versus Week 3:** the aligned 853-user outcomes and pairwise list overlaps are measured. Week 2 uses genre similarity from three earlier liked movies; Week 3 uses ratings from the earlier active-user history and other users. Raw score scales differ, and the comparison retains other users' full histories.

Further evidence before a broad quality or business claim would require additional held-out targets or splits, a global time-aware protocol if temporal causality matters, and direct tests of cold-start handling or alternative algorithms. No user or business outcomes were measured.

Sources: machine-readable files in ../results/phase3_*, ../results/phase4_evaluation.json, ../results/phase5_aligned_comparison.json, and ../results/phase5_cases.json.

# AGENTS.md

## Purpose

This repository supports coursework and experiments for the LLM4Rec / Recommender Systems course.

AI assistants should help accelerate implementation and understanding, but should not replace
the student's reasoning, experimental design, or interpretation.

## Core workflow

For experimental tasks, prefer this structure:

1. Define one clear question.
2. Establish a baseline.
3. Change one controlled factor at a time when possible.
4. Record code, configuration, random seed, and data assumptions.
5. Produce evidence: metrics, plots, tables, or error analysis.
6. State only claims supported by the evidence.
7. Note limitations and possible next improvements.

## Coding rules

- Prefer simple, readable code over unnecessary abstraction.
- Keep experiments reproducible.
- Do not silently change datasets or evaluation protocols.
- Avoid data leakage.
- Save generated figures and results in clearly named output folders.
- Explain non-obvious design choices in README files.
- Do not fabricate experimental results.

## Course repository rules

- Weekly coursework belongs under `weekXX/`.
- Final-project work belongs under `capstone/`.
- Use feature branches and pull requests for meaningful assignments.
- Do not commit secrets, API keys, credentials, model weights, or private/confidential data.
- Do not copy proprietary company code into this repository.

## Visualization workflow

Before plotting:
- inspect the dataset structure and dtypes;
- check missing values or obvious schema issues.

After plotting:
- verify labels, units, legends, and source data;
- confirm that the visual supports the stated conclusion.

## Writing style

Use concise technical English in repository documentation.
Prefer evidence-first explanations over broad claims.

# Week 3 final evidence

The final application uses **raw co-rated-only cosine**. Phase 4 overlap confidence is an analysis-only experiment. Scores from Week 2 genre cosine and Week 3 predicted ratings are not directly comparable.

## Implementation and reliability

| Item | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Users / movies / ratings | 943 / 1,682 / 100,000 |
| Rating and missing convention | Observed 1–5; zero internally means unrated |
| Final similarity | Raw co-rated-only cosine; zero for no overlap or zero norm |
| User-Based neighborhood / output | Up to 20 positive neighbors / Top-5 |
| Median co-rated count, user / item pairs | 10 / 1 |
| Pair fraction with ≤2 co-ratings, user / item | 14.29% / 60.38% |
| High-cosine (≥0.9) pairs with ≤2 co-ratings, user / item | 11.94% / 47.70% |

The pair counts are 444,153 unique user pairs and 1,413,721 unique item pairs. Small overlap does not make cosine mathematically incorrect; it limits how much evidence supports that value.

## Held-out evaluation

Phase 3 used 911 users, each with the most recent rating ≥4 held out and at least 20 remaining ratings.

| Method | Hits | HitRate@5 | MRR@5 | Fewer than five |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Raw User-Based | 9 | 0.99% | 0.004848 | 0 |
| Raw Item-Based | 0 | 0.00% | 0.000000 | 0 |

The controlled overlap-confidence experiment used the same 911 users. T=10 was primary; T=5 and T=20 were sensitivity checks.

| Setting | User hits / HR@5 / MRR@5 | Item hits / HR@5 / MRR@5 | Median contributing overlap, user / item |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| T5 | 11 / 1.21% / 0.005562 | 0 / 0.00% / 0.000000 | 7 / 1 |
| T10 | 10 / 1.10% / 0.004958 | 0 / 0.00% / 0.000000 | 14 / 1 |
| T20 | 5 / 0.55% / 0.002506 | 0 / 0.00% / 0.000000 | 25 / 1 |

The T=10 User-Based gain was one net hit (10 gained, 9 lost relative to raw), and T=20 fell below raw. Item-Based remained at zero. No weighted setting was adopted in the application.

## Efficiency

| Dimension | Full square including self | Unique unordered excluding self |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Users | 889,249 | 444,153 |
| Items | 2,829,124 | 1,413,721 |

Phase 3 timed complete raw on-demand calls on users [2, 3, 1, 405, 943], with two warmups and five measured calls each: User-Based mean/median 1.588/1.398 ms; Item-Based 388.484/332.312 ms. Full pair counts and on-demand runtimes answer different questions; neither predicts general scalability.

## Aligned Week 2 versus Week 3

The 853-user primary comparison reuses Phase 3 held-out targets. It requires at least 20 user ratings and three positive profile movies with timestamps strictly earlier than the target. Of the 911 Phase 3 users, 57 lack 20 earlier ratings and one further user lacks three earlier positives. The same earlier-only active-user row and unseen-movie candidate pool are used for all methods. Other users retain full histories; this is not a global chronological split.

| Method | Users | Hits | HitRate@5 | MRR@5 | Fewer than five |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Week 2 three-movie binary-genre profile | 853 | 20 | 2.34% | 0.010219 | 0 |
| Week 3 User-Based raw | 853 | 12 | 1.41% | 0.007562 | 0 |
| Week 3 Item-Based raw | 853 | 0 | 0.00% | 0.000000 | 0 |

| Top-5 pair | Mean shared movies out of 5 | Users with zero overlap |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Content / User-Based | 0.081 | 785/853 (92.03%) |
| Content / Item-Based | 0.001 | 852/853 (99.88%) |
| User-Based / Item-Based | 0.000 | 853/853 (100.00%) |

Low list overlap describes different rankings; it does not establish which list is more relevant. The 853-user results should not be substituted for Phase 3's 911-user results because the active-user history was restricted to earlier interactions.

## Representative cases

### User 79: Content-Based succeeds; both CF methods miss

Earlier ratings: 53. Profile: I Shot Andy Warhol (1996) (4/5); Star Trek: First Contact (1996) (4/5); Shanghai Triad (Yao a yao yao dao waipo qiao) (1995) (4/5). Held-out: Twelve Monkeys (1995) (5/5).

| Rank | Week 2 profile | Week 3 User-Based | Week 3 Item-Based |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Ben-Hur (1959) | Usual Suspects, The (1995) | King of New York (1990) |
| 2 | Twelve Monkeys (1995) | From Dusk Till Dawn (1996) | Mamma Roma (1962) |
| 3 | Mad City (1997) | Braveheart (1995) | Police Story 4: Project S (Chao ji ji hua) (1993) |
| 4 | Day the Earth Stood Still, The (1951) | Birdcage, The (1996) | Fire on the Mountain (1996) |
| 5 | Perfect World, A (1993) | Brothers McMullen, The (1995) | Daniel Defoe's Robinson Crusoe (1996) |

The held-out movie has Drama and Sci-Fi tags. Drama appears in two profile movies and Sci-Fi in one, giving Week 2 a genre cosine of 0.802 and rank 2. User-Based predicts 3.2 from five contributing neighbors while its Top-5 scores are 5; Item-Based predicts 4.021 for the held-out movie while its Top-5 scores are at least 4.313. The pair counts are 444,153 unique user pairs and 1,413,721 unique item pairs. Small overlap does not make cosine mathematically incorrect; it limits how much evidence supports that value.

Phase 3 used 911 users, each with the most recent rating ≥4 held out and at least 20 remaining ratings.

The 853-user primary comparison reuses Phase 3 held-out targets. It requires at least 20 user ratings and three positive profile movies with timestamps strictly earlier than the target. Of the 911 Phase 3 users, 57 lack 20 earlier ratings and one further user lacks three earlier positives. The same earlier-only active-user row and unseen-movie candidate pool are used for all methods. Other users retain full histories; this is not a global chronological split.

| Method | Users | Hits | HitRate@5 | MRR@5 | Fewer than five |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Week 2 three-movie binary-genre profile | 853 | 20 | 2.34% | 0.010219 | 0 |
| Week 3 User-Based raw | 853 | 12 | 1.41% | 0.007562 | 0 |
| Week 3 Item-Based raw | 853 | 0 | 0.00% | 0.000000 | 0 |

| Top-5 pair | Mean shared movies out of 5 | Users with zero overlap |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Content / User-Based | 0.081 | 785/853 (92.03%) |
| Content / Item-Based | 0.001 | 852/853 (99.88%) |
| User-Based / Item-Based | 0.000 | 853/853 (100.00%) |

Low list overlap describes different rankings; it does not establish which list is more relevant. The 853-user results should not be substituted for Phase 3's 911-user results because the active-user history was restricted to earlier interactions.

## Representative cases

### User 79: Content-Based succeeds; both CF methods miss

Earlier ratings: 53. Profile: I Shot Andy Warhol (1996) (4/5); Star Trek: First Contact (1996) (4/5); Shanghai Triad (Yao a yao yao dao waipo qiao) (1995) (4/5). Held-out: Twelve Monkeys (1995) (5/5).

| Rank | Week 2 profile | Week 3 User-Based | Week 3 Item-Based |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Ben-Hur (1959) | Usual Suspects, The (1995) | King of New York (1990) |
| 2 | Twelve Monkeys (1995) | From Dusk Till Dawn (1996) | Mamma Roma (1962) |
| 3 | Mad City (1997) | Braveheart (1995) | Police Story 4: Project S (Chao ji ji hua) (1993) |
| 4 | Day the Earth Stood Still, The (1951) | Birdcage, The (1996) | Fire on the Mountain (1996) |
| 5 | Perfect World, A (1993) | Brothers McMullen, The (1995) | Daniel Defoe's Robinson Crusoe (1996) |

The held-out movie has Drama and Sci-Fi tags. Drama appears in two profile movies and Sci-Fi in one, giving Week 2 a genre cosine of 0.802 and rank 2. User-Based predicts 3.2 from five contributing neighbors while its Top-5 scores are 5; Item-Based predicts 4.021 for the held-out movie while its Top-5 scores are at least 4.313. This explains the list difference through observed features and ratings.

### User 20: User-Based succeeds; Content-Based misses

Earlier ratings: 45. Profile: Jurassic Park (1993) (4/5); Lost World: Jurassic Park, The (1997) (4/5); Braveheart (1995) (5/5). Held-out: Searching for Bobby Fischer (1993) (5/5).

| Rank | Week 2 profile | Week 3 User-Based | Week 3 Item-Based |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Stargate (1994) | Shanghai Triad (Yao a yao yao dao waipo qiao) (1995) | Coldblooded (1995) |
| 2 | Star Trek: First Contact (1996) | Dead Man Walking (1995) | Rough Magic (1995) |
| 3 | Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country (1991) | Postino, Il (1994) | Turning, The (1992) |
| 4 | Star Trek: The Wrath of Khan (1982) | Crumb (1994) | Ill Gotten Gains (1997) |
| 5 | Star Trek III: The Search for Spock (1984) | Searching for Bobby Fischer (1993) | Intimate Relations (1996) |

The profile is dominated by Action, Adventure, and Sci-Fi; the held-out movie is Drama only, with genre cosine 0.224. User-Based ranks it fifth at a predicted 5, but that prediction is from one neighbor whose similarity rests on one shared rating. The hit is real under the protocol and has weak support. Item-Based gives the target 3.091, below its Top-5 cutoff.

### User 2: Item-Based failure example

Earlier ratings: 57. Profile: Air Force One (1997) (4/5); Fly Away Home (1996) (4/5); Good Will Hunting (1997) (5/5). Held-out: As Good As It Gets (1997) (5/5).

| Rank | Week 2 profile | Week 3 User-Based | Week 3 Item-Based |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | GoldenEye (1995) | Maltese Falcon, The (1941) | They Made Me a Criminal (1939) |
| 2 | Apollo 13 (1995) | It Happened One Night (1934) | Shadows (Cienie) (1988) |
| 3 | Free Willy 2: The Adventure Home (1995) | Manchurian Candidate, The (1962) | The Courtyard (1995) |
| 4 | Outbreak (1995) | Babe (1995) | Yankee Zulu (1994) |
| 5 | Free Willy (1993) | From Dusk Till Dawn (1996) | Hostile Intentions (1994) |

The held-out Comedy/Drama movie has genre cosine 0.316 against the three-movie profile. User-Based predicts 5 from one neighbor but does not rank it in Top-5. Item-Based predicts 3.807 from 57 positive item similarities; its Top-5 instead scores 4.5 for movies with only one observed rating each. Those winning similarities have one co-rating. This is a concrete sparse-item ranking failure under the protocol.

## Homework question coverage and remaining evidence

- **A. User-Based versus Item-Based quality and efficiency:** measured both held-out retrieval and local on-demand runtime. In these protocols User-Based hit more targets and ran faster. The dataset has more items than users, so a full item-pair matrix also has more pairs. These observations do not establish general superiority.
- **B. Missing-value strategies:** co-rated-only uses only observed data and is simple, but the measured overlap distributions show unreliable-looking high similarities from few shared ratings. Overlap-confidence weighting was measured: it improved User-Based support, had small threshold-sensitive hit changes, and did not resolve Item-Based's zero hits. **Mean imputation** could provide dense vectors but can introduce average-rating bias and must preserve the original observed mask; **matrix factorization** could learn latent representations from sparse data but needs training, validation, and more computation. The latter two were not implemented or empirically compared.
- **C. Cold start and sparsity:** without a rated item, a new user has no co-rated entries for User-Based similarity and no rated items to seed Item-Based scores. An unrated new movie also lacks item co-ratings. The observed MovieLens sparsity and low-overlap statistics support the reliability concern; the dataset has no zero-history users for an empirical cold-start test. Confidence weighting does not create new interactions.
- **D. Week 2 versus Week 3:** the aligned 853-user outcomes and pairwise list overlaps are measured. Week 2 uses genre similarity from three earlier liked movies; Week 3 uses ratings from the earlier active-user history and other users. Raw score scales differ, and the comparison retains other users' full histories.

Further evidence before a broad quality or business claim would require additional held-out targets or splits, a global time-aware protocol if temporal causality matters, and direct tests of cold-start handling or alternative algorithms. No user or business outcomes were measured.

Sources: machine-readable files in ../results/phase3_*, ../results/phase4_evaluation.json, ../results/phase5_aligned_comparison.json, and ../results/phase5_cases.json.

Phase 5 is complete. The application still uses **raw co-rated-only cosine**; overlap weighting remains an isolated experiment. I did not change the teacher baseline, datasets, or CF algorithms, and did not commit or push.

The aligned comparison reused Phase 3’s held-out positive movies. It evaluated **853 of the 911** eligible users: 57 lacked 20 ratings before the held-out interaction, and one more lacked three earlier positive movies for the Week 2 profile. Each method excluded the active user’s earlier-seen movies.

| Method | HitRate@5 | MRR@5 | Hits | Fewer than 5 results |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Week 2 three-movie content profile | 2.34% | 0.010219 | 20 | 0 |
| Week 3 User-Based CF | 1.41% | 0.007562 | 12 | 0 |
| Week 3 Item-Based CF | 0.00% | 0.000000 | 0 | 0 |

| Top-5 pair | Mean shared movies out of 5 | Users with no shared movie |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Content / User-Based | 0.081 | 92.03% |
| Content / Item-Based | 0.001 | 99.88% |
| User-Based / Item-Based | 0.000 | 100.00% |

Three cases show what the aggregate results conceal. For **user 79**, a profile with two Drama movies and one Sci-Fi movie ranked the held-out *Twelve Monkeys* second; both CF lists missed it. For **user 20**, User-Based ranked the held-out *Searching for Bobby Fischer* fifth while the Action/Adventure/Sci-Fi-heavy content profile missed it—but that CF prediction came from one neighbor similarity supported by just **one shared rating**. For **user 2**, Item-Based missed the held-out *As Good As It Gets*; its winning recommendations were movies with one observed rating and item similarities supported by one co-rating. The input profiles, held-out movies, **all three Top-5 lists for each case**, and supporting scores are in [the case study](</Users/chenfengru/LLM4Rec-Course-codex/week03/collaborative-filtering-movie-recommender/analysis/week03_final_evidence.md>).

The [final evidence table](</Users/chenfengru/LLM4Rec-Course-codex/week03/collaborative-filtering-movie-recommender/results/week03_final_evidence.json>) consolidates implementation, reliability, evaluation, efficiency, and comparison results. Key reliability figures are median overlap **10** for user pairs and **1** for item pairs; **14.29%** and **60.38%**, respectively, have at most two co-ratings. Phase 3’s 911-user baseline had 9 User-Based hits and 0 Item-Based hits. The T=5/10/20 weighting results remain sensitivity evidence, not the chosen method. The measured on-demand means were **1.588 ms** for User-Based and **388.484 ms** for Item-Based on the fixed benchmark users; these local timings do not establish general scalability.

The collected evidence covers the homework’s User-Based versus Item-Based quality and efficiency question, sparsity, and the aligned Week 2 versus Week 3 comparison. The missing-value discussion can distinguish measured co-rated-only and overlap-weighted behavior from **conceptual** mean-imputation and matrix-factorization trade-offs; the latter two have no empirical results here. Cold start can be explained from the algorithms, but this dataset provides no zero-history cohort to measure it.

Before making broader quality or business claims, evidence is still missing from additional holdouts or splits, a global chronological evaluation, and direct tests of cold-start handling or alternative algorithms. The comparison retains other users’ full histories, so it is not a global time-aware split. Phase 5 scripts and machine-readable outputs are saved in [analysis](</Users/chenfengru/LLM4Rec-Course-codex/week03/collaborative-filtering-movie-recommender/analysis/phase5_compare.mjs>) and [results](</Users/chenfengru/LLM4Rec-Course-codex/week03/collaborative-filtering-movie-recommender/results/phase5_aligned_comparison.json>). I stopped before report writing and will wait for your approval.
